Ced

Ced is the MixOS Editor: a desktop editor over the edit Bus service (editd). A document lives in the service, not in the window, so several people and agents can edit it at once. Ced shows their carets, selections and changes as they happen, and keeps typing instant by applying it locally first.

Running

ced [PATH[:LINE[:COL]]…]   open paths (in the running ced, if there is one)
ced --headless             every command, no window
ced --service NAME         register as NAME (tests)

Without the edit service, Ced shows a clear waiting state within three seconds and posts a desktop toast. The document opens automatically when the service registers on the Bus. Ced registers on the Bus as ced; a second ced hands its paths to the first and exits.

The window

  • Menus, shortcuts and Bus actions are one registry. Every action has the same id in the menu bar, as a shortcut (Notepad++ conventions: see Help › Keyboard Shortcuts) and in ced.execute {id}.
  • Tabs show unsaved changes, and ◆ when another origin edited the document since you last looked at it.
  • The notice strip keeps edits that could not be applied (re-insert them at the caret or dismiss them), and a document that lost its connection to the service (keep your copy or take the service's). Warnings and errors use desktop notification toasts, with the status line as a fallback if notifications are unavailable. Identical messages appear at most once every five seconds.
  • Find (Ctrl+F, Ctrl+H) runs in the service, so it searches the shared text, not a local copy.
  • Markdown and commit messages wrap; code scrolls sideways.
  • Problems (Ctrl+Shift+M) lists the document's diagnostics.
  • View › Theme picks this window's scheme, style and mode.

Bus

ced.* (schema ced.v1): ping, info, open, new, tabs, focus, show (restore, raise and focus the window through compd), state, type, select, execute, actions, wait, layout, stats, diagnostics, problems, plus app.describe and app.quit; and the toolkit drive commands (ced.ui.*, ced.window, ced.window.state; see driving an app). A Bus caller's edits carry its own origin (agent:ced.<caller>), so they show as an agent's, and its undo is its own.

ced.actions lists the editor's actions. Run one with ced.execute {id, params?}; params holds optional tab (or buffer) and args, for example {id: "file.save_as", params: {tab: 1, args: {path: "/work/notes.md"}}}. Without a selector, the action uses the active tab. An unknown action returns rc 10 UNKNOWN_ACTION. Each run is published on ced.action.executed.

Source

  • crates/documents: the engine, with no UI toolkit. Open documents (one tab per buffer of the edit service, each a mirror with its editing model, highlighting and diagnostics), every action, the ced.* commands and their waiters, reconnects and reattaches, the session.
  • src/: the shell. The Bus thread, ced --headless, and the egui window around the shared editor text view.

The source is apps/ced.

Tests

cargo test -p documents -p ced: the engine's unit and golden command-fixture tests, and tests/window.rs, which runs the real window against the fake edit service in-process (no Bus): typing reaches the service, and two offscreen snapshots. Regenerate them with UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 and look at them before committing.

Not yet

  • Macros and the Output panel's content.
  • Linting Mix files on save (the Problems panel shows diagnostics other tools send with ced.diagnostics).
  • Reading the primary selection over the Bus: it is answered as empty, since the toolkit cannot read it on demand. (In the window, selecting text offers it as the primary selection and middle-click pastes it where you click.)

Macro Bus commands

The shared macro Bus surface uses this process's catalogue and runner. Subscribe to <service>.macros.finished for completion, where service is the instance’s registered Bus name (for example term-1234 for a second Term instance). Commands keep the app’s canonical prefix, such as ced.macros.run.

CommandArgumentsResult
ced.macros.list{}Catalogue and diagnostics
ced.macros.reload{}Catalogue and diagnostics
ced.macros.run{id}Acceptance and run number
ced.macros.status{}Current or last run
ced.macros.output{}Retained output and dropped flag
ced.macros.stop{}Whether termination was requested
ced.macros.new{title}Create a user per-app macro; {id,title,path,scanned}, without opening an editor; scan failures add warning and preserve the file

Logging: --debug[=LEVEL] and live Bus controls are described in live application logging.

Mail documents

Ced recognises an opening --- block containing mail-* headers. Valid mail documents open with a compact header form above the body editor. From is a plain address; Email checks identities when you send. Cc, Bcc and Reply-To buttons reveal optional rows. Thread headers are read-only. Attach… chooses multiple paths; each attachment chip can be removed. Each committed header field edit is one undo step; typing in a field coalesces until focus leaves it or a command commits it. The last 256 header undo steps are retained. Execution events are published on commit, not per keystroke. Header undo history is separate from the edit service's body history: Undo exhausts header edits first, then undoes body edits. Redo restores header edits before body edits.

The native edit service holds the body in a scratch buffer, seeded at revision zero, so Undo cannot remove the initial body. Ced keeps the headers with the tab. Save and Save As assemble the document with maildoc::write: LF line ends, sorted headers, omitted empty headers and canonical trailing body whitespace. An invalid field refuses the save without touching the file. A file changed on disk also refuses the save; use Save As or reopen it. Saving keeps the path as opened, including relative paths and symlinks; canonical paths are compared only to detect conflicting external edits. A deleted file is recreated. Body dirty checks use the same LF and trailing whitespace normalisation as the writer. A lost scratch is seeded from the live mirror text, retaining unsaved body edits. A detached copy remains available separately. Session mail tabs retain their path, body recovery id and header state. Session files use private (0600) atomic replacements. After a crash or restart they reattach the body by recovery id, preserving unsaved edits; if editd no longer has it, Ced reopens the file. Mail bodies belonging to session tabs are excluded from the Recovered prompt. Save As retains the mail kind. Reload from Disk requires closing and reopening the mail tab, so it cannot silently replace separately edited headers.

File ▸ Send saves first, then asks Email to send the absolute document path. The tab shows Sending… until Email replies. A second Send is refused while one is in flight. Each Email call has 120 seconds; the separate registration wait is 10 seconds. Email's refusal retains its code and message verbatim. An uncertain transport outcome says the mail may have been sent; ced never retries it. Opening a document never sends anything. Ced knows no accounts, JMAP or sending limits.

Agents use ced.execute {id:"file.send", params:{tab:1}}; the reply waits for the save and Email's outcome. ced.state returns body text and, on mail tabs, mail:{headers,sending,saving,notice}. Update one field by changing the returned headers and calling ced.execute {id:"mail.headers", params:{tab:1, args:{headers:HEADERS}}}. Thread headers cannot be changed through that action. Send is unavailable on ordinary text and Bus-message documents (to plus command), which remain plain text for Workshop. A refused mail candidate also opens as unchanged text, with maildoc's exact refusal beside it for repair. Mail tabs keep header edits in this process. Exit refuses while a mail tab is dirty or a save/Send is in flight; save or explicitly close the tab first. Mail scratch buffers, including those still seeding, are force-closed on exit. Unsaved headers still block Exit while the body is seeding. Ordinary unanswered edit requests do not consume the shutdown drain allowance; force-closes have a separate bounded wait, preserving time for deregistration, closing refusals and session persistence. A save waiting for body edits holds intent only: it assembles the latest body when the edits drain. Body typing continues while a plain Save is parked and pauses during the file write. A parked Send immediately shows Sending… and freezes body edits, so text typed after Send cannot join that message. Undo and Redo refuse with a notice explaining that Save or Send is waiting for body edits while either operation is parked. Close and Exit cancel that intent; reconnection cancels it with a notice. Same-frame header edits are applied before Save or Send. Header controls and Attach are disabled during save or Send. Non-UTF-8 attachment paths are refused. Optional header fields default when omitted by an agent. Validation refusals use INVALID_ARGUMENT; busy or cancelled operations and disk conflicts use CONFLICT. File I/O failures use INTERNAL.

Empty front matter is ordinary text. Only actual mail-* keys make a mail candidate; continuation lines do not. Mail with a UTF-8 BOM stays text and shows a notice explaining how to remove the BOM.

ced.dialog {} reads the open modal as {dialog: {kind, title, buttons: [{id, label, role}], body?, path?, status?} | null}. {open: null} closes it as Escape does; {answer: <button id>} presses a listed button. No modal returns NO_DIALOG; a bad button returns ARGUMENT. Help opens with {open: "keys"} or {open: "about"}. Recovered rows include buffer ids: answer open or discard with {buffer: "..."}. Help and recovery close with done. Path dialogs accept path; goto accepts text. A refused dirty-mail Bus close leaves no modal behind.
